{
  "description": "A fulfillment worker restarts after a Stripe payment commits remotely but before the acknowledgment is recorded locally, causing the worker to lose in-memory state and retry the payment without an idempotency key, resulting in a duplicate charge and violating unit economics.",
  "rationale": "The prior experiment with kill_worker + missing_idempotency_key confirmed duplicateDollars of $300k and r04-network-idempotency violations, but r10-unit-economics remained unproven. This hypothesis tests whether the same duplicate-charge scenario directly violates r10-unit-economics (cost-per-transaction limits), which the previous evidence suggested but did not conclusively prove.",
  "expectedInvariant": "r10-unit-economics",
  "interventions": ["kill_worker", "missing_idempotency_key"],
  "confidence": 0.85
}

hypothesis.description: A fulfillment worker restarts after a Stripe payment commits remotely but before the acknowledgment is recorded locally, causing the worker to lose in-memory state and potentially retry the payment without an idempotency key, resulting in a duplicate charge.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This experiment tests whether the system violates the idempotency invariant when a worker crashes after a remote commit but before local acknowledgment. It distinguishes between scenarios where idempotency keys are properly used versus lost during restart, and whether the payment service correctly deduplicates retries.

interventions.description: A worker crashes and loses in-memory state; the agent must restart and recover.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

interventionSequence.hypothesis: A fulfillment worker restarts after a Stripe payment commits remotely but before the acknowledgment is recorded locally, causing the worker to lose in-memory state and potentially retry the payment without an idempotency key, resulting in a duplicate charge.

hypothesis.description: When a payment response is lost and the agent retries without an idempotency key, the Stripe Payment API accepts both requests as distinct charges, but the agent's reported cost metric reflects only the single logical operation, violating unit economics invariants.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This experiment tests whether the agent's cost accounting correctly captures all physical work performed (including duplicate charges) versus only the intended logical work. It distinguishes between a pure idempotency violation (r04) and a cost metric fidelity violation (r10) by observing if duplicate charges occur and whether the reported cost metric includes them.

interventions.description: Payment commits but its response is lost, leaving the agent unsure whether the charge succeeded.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

hypothesis.description: When a worker crashes mid-payment and recovers without a checkpoint, the agent retries the payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge. The reported cost metric reflects only the logical operation count, violating unit economics.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: Experiment 1 proved duplicate charges occur when responses are lost without idempotency keys. This experiment tests whether worker crashes (which lose in-memory state) combined with missing idempotency keys produce the same invariant violation, distinguishing crash-recovery replay from network-only retries as the root cause.

interventions.description: A worker crashes and loses in-memory state; the agent must restart and recover.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

interventionSequence.hypothesis: When a worker crashes mid-payment and recovers without a checkpoint, the agent retries the payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge. The reported cost metric reflects only the logical operation count, violating unit economics.

hypothesis.description: After a worker crash and restart, the agent loses in-memory state and retries a Stripe payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge that the later compensation step fails to reverse because it only knows about the original transaction.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This experiment combines kill_worker (simulating worker restart with state loss) and missing_idempotency_key (causing duplicate charge on retry) to test whether the compensation step can resolve both charges. The r05-distributed-sagas invariant requires all side effects to be compensated, but the compensation logic may only track the first transaction ID.

  "description": "A payment request times out (Stripe Payment API failure mode: 'Timeout with ambiguous state'), the AI Agent restarts after a worker crash and loses in-memory state without a checkpointed idempotency key, and upon recovery retries the payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge.",

hypothesis.description: After an upstream timeout, the payment worker retries the refund request, but the original request had already been committed by the Legacy Payment API before the timeout occurred. The retry (regardless of idempotency key presence) triggers a duplicate refund because the Legacy Payment API has no idempotency guarantees and always produces duplicate side effects on retries.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: The previous experiment tested retries without an idempotency key (missing_idempotency_key) and confirmed duplicate refunds. This experiment distinguishes whether the root cause is specifically the missing idempotency key or the fundamental lack of idempotency guarantees in the Legacy Payment API by testing if duplicates occur even when the original request was already committed before the timeout (using delay_response to simulate the timeout after commit).

interventions.description: The response is delayed beyond the timeout, so the agent may retry.

response.text:
{
  "description": "A fulfillment worker restarts after Stripe commits a charge but before recording the acknowledgement locally; upon recovery, the worker queries Stripe for the charge status, and the delayed response from Stripe causes the worker to timeout and incorrectly assume the charge failed, triggering a retry without an idempotency key and causing a duplicate charge.",
  "rationale": "The prior experiment demonstrated that killing the worker after commit without idempotency causes duplicate charges (r04-network-idempotency violated). This experiment introduces a delayed Stripe response (via delay_response) during the worker's post-recovery status check, creating a new failure path: the worker times out on the status query, assumes failure, and retries without idempotency. This distinguishes between 'worker loses acknowledgement' vs 'worker misinterprets ambiguous status after recovery' as root causes for duplicate charges.",
  "expectedInvariant": "r04-network-idempotency",
  "interventions": ["kill_worker", "delay_response", "missing_idempotency_key"],
  "confidence": 0.85
}

hypothesis.description: A fulfillment worker restarts after Stripe commits a charge but before the acknowledgement is recorded locally; upon recovery, the worker retries the payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This experiment tests whether the worker's recovery logic correctly handles the 'commit-before-ack' window by either using idempotency keys or checking Stripe's transaction status before retrying, distinguishing between a correct idempotent design and one that loses state and retries blindly.

interventions.description: A worker crashes and loses in-memory state; the agent must restart and recover.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

interventionSequence.hypothesis: A fulfillment worker restarts after Stripe commits a charge but before the acknowledgement is recorded locally; upon recovery, the worker retries the payment without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge.

hypothesis.description: When the payment response is lost after commit, the agent retries without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge that the reported cost metric does not reflect as additional work.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This isolates whether the cost metric accounts for retries that produce duplicate external side effects, distinguishing between a metric that tracks only agent-internal effort versus one that captures total economic cost.

interventions.description: Payment commits but its response is lost, leaving the agent unsure whether the charge succeeded.
A payment request has no idempotency key, so a retry can cause a duplicate charge.

hypothesis.description: A worker crash after Stripe payment commit but before checkpoint persistence causes the agent to lose in-memory state; upon restart it does not replay the committed payment and the later compensation step only reverses its own side effect, leaving the Stripe charge unresolved.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This distinguishes whether the saga's compensation logic correctly accounts for side effects committed before a checkpoint loss (lost_state) versus only compensating effects recorded after recovery. The kill_worker triggers the restart; lose_state models the missing checkpoint; the invariant r05-distributed-sagas asserts every completed side effect must be compensated or confirmed.

This experiment tests whether the same duplicate charge occurs when the agent retains state but loses the Stripe response (network failure) and retries without an idempotency key, isolating the idempotency guarantee from the checkpointing guarantee.

hypothesis.description: When a worker crashes and loses in-memory state, the agent restarts and recovers from the last checkpoint. If the last checkpoint was written before a Stripe payment request was sent, the agent may replay the payment request without an idempotency key, causing a duplicate charge.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: This experiment tests the interaction between durable checkpointing (Storage contract) and the Stripe Payment API's requirement for idempotency keys to prevent duplicate charges. It distinguishes whether the violation stems from checkpoint timing (checkpoint written before payment request) versus the agent's failure to include idempotency keys on retry. If the agent uses idempotency keys correctly, the invariant holds even with checkpoint replay.

hypothesis.description: When a Stripe payment response is dropped after commit, the agent restarts from a checkpoint before the payment was sent, replays the request without an idempotency key, and causes a duplicate charge.
hypothesis.experimentRationale: The prior experiment tested worker crash without network loss and observed zero duplicate dollars. This experiment isolates the case where the payment commits but the response is lost (drop_response), which creates ambiguous state that checkpoint recovery cannot distinguish from 'never sent.' It directly tests whether the invariant r10-unit-economics holds under combined network and recovery failure.
